% ── Custom symbols ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\newcommand{\bigbowtie}{\mathop{\triangleright\!\!\!\triangleleft}}
% Contact form (pseudo-Hermitian structure) symbol.  NOTE: paper-specific —
% per this file's header, such macros belong in a paper's generated preamble,
% not in the shared template; left here pending migration to the content repo.
% \varTheta is the upright capital theta, visually distinct from the
% lowercase contact-form letter θ and from italic \Theta.
% Some recent TeX Live distributions predefine \varTheta; redefine safely.
\providecommand{\varTheta}{}
\renewcommand{\varTheta}{\mathrm{\Theta}}
% ── Reeb / compound-macro stubs: REMOVED 2026-08-22 ───────────────────────────
% This block defined 16 macros whose names are author typos — a control
% sequence written without the space that separates it from the next token
% (\pi c_s -> \pic_s, \xi Z -> \xiZ, \lambda L -> \lambdaL). Defining the
% glued name makes the page compile, and that is the problem: it converts a
% loud failure into silently-wrong printed mathematics. Two did exactly that.
% \pic expanded to \pi, so `2\pic_s` printed 2\pi_s and the sound speed
% vanished from a Hawking-temperature denominator that the same block's prose
% writes correctly as 2\pi c_s. \xid expanded to \xi_d, so
% `\mathcal{L}_\xid\alpha` printed the Lie derivative along a subscripted
% field with no argument instead of \mathcal{L}_\xi d\alpha. \xid, \xiZ and
% \xiA were commented here as "Reeb vector field variants"; no such notation
% is registered in folio/quantum-observable-universe/notation/, so the
% comment documents three typos as though they were notation.
% Every source site is fixed; do not restore these. If one reappears, the
% undefined-control-sequence error is the correct outcome — fix the .md.
\newcommand{\pp}{p}             % prime p — used in p-adic content (\mathbb{Q}_\pp, \mathbb{F}_\pp, v_\pp). Italic per math-mode convention; not \mathfrak{p} which is reserved for the proton (CLAUDE.md §7aa).
% \unicode{codepoint} — ConTeXt-style; used in appendix-surreals for ☉ (U+2609)
\newcommand{\unicode}[1]{\ensuremath{\odot}}
% Young-diagram macro stub (ytableau not loaded; renders partition as list)
\newcommand{\yng}[1]{{\scriptsize[#1]}}

% Unicode maths symbols that appear in plain text (outside $ … $)

\geometry{
  left=0.8in, right=1.5in, top=0.8in, bottom=0.8in,
  marginparwidth=1.1in, marginparsep=0.15in,
}
\usepackage{marginnote}
\renewcommand*{\marginfont}{\scriptsize}

% ── Suppress hyperref math-in-bookmark warnings ─────────────────────────────
% Math in theorem titles generates "Token not allowed in PDF string" warnings.
% These are harmless (hyperref strips the math for bookmarks) but noisy.
\hypersetup{pdfencoding=auto, psdextra}
\pdfstringdefDisableCommands{%
  \def\({}%
  \def\){}%
  \let\mathbf\relax
  \let\mathrm\relax
  \let\mathcal\relax
  \let\mathfrak\relax
  \let\mathbb\relax
  \let\mathscr\relax
  \let\boldsymbol\relax
  \let\textstyle\relax
  \let\Sigma\relax
  \let\Delta\relax
  \let\not\relax
  \let\to\relax
  \let\bigbowtie\relax
}
% Silence the "Token not allowed" warnings entirely — they are
% informational and produce correct bookmarks regardless.
\makeatletter
\renewcommand{\HyPsd@Warning}[1]{}
\makeatother

% ── Book-style chapter / section formatting ────────────────────────────────
% Chapter page breaks are handled by the renderer (it prepends \clearpage
% to every \input chapter — see content/pipeline/render-latex.ts
% renderChapter). The chapter numeral here is rendered very large,
% left-aligned, with whitespace to the right — book convention. The
% chapter title sits below the numeral. Sections and subsections stay
% compact with normal-size fonts.
\titleclass{\chapter}{straight}       % renderer-driven page breaks
\titleformat{\chapter}[display]%
  {\normalfont\bfseries\raggedright}%
  {%
    \fontsize{96pt}{96pt}\selectfont\bfseries\thechapter%
    \hfill%
  }%
  {2em}%
  {\Huge\bfseries\raggedright}%
\titlespacing*{\chapter}{0pt}{0pt}{2em}

% Unnumbered chapters (introduction, glossary, appendices) — same display
% block but no large numeral, since \chapter* has no number.
\titleformat{name=\chapter,numberless}[block]%
  {\normalfont\Huge\bfseries\raggedright}%
  {}%
  {0pt}%
  {\Huge\bfseries\raggedright}%
\titlespacing*{name=\chapter,numberless}{0pt}{0pt}{2em}

\titleformat{\section}[hang]{\normalsize\bfseries}{%
  \thesection}{0.5em}{}
\titlespacing*{\section}{0pt}{1.0ex plus 0.3ex minus 0.2ex}{0.5ex plus 0.1ex}

\titleformat{\subsection}[hang]{\normalsize\bfseries}{%
  \thesubsection}{0.5em}{}
\titlespacing*{\subsection}{0pt}{0.8ex plus 0.3ex minus 0.1ex}{0.4ex plus 0.1ex}

% Show only chapters and sections in the table of contents — no subsections.
\setcounter{tocdepth}{1}

% ── Theorem environments ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
% Condensed spacing to reduce vertical footprint
\newtheoremstyle{condensed}
  {0.8ex plus 0.2ex minus 0.1ex} % Space above
  {0.8ex plus 0.2ex minus 0.1ex} % Space below
  {\itshape}                     % Body font (italic for theorems)
  {}                             % Indent amount
  {\bfseries}                    % Theorem head font
  {.}                            % Punctuation after theorem head
  {0.5em}                        % Space after theorem head
  {}                             % Theorem head spec

\newtheoremstyle{condenseddef}
  {0.8ex plus 0.2ex minus 0.1ex} % Space above
  {0.8ex plus 0.2ex minus 0.1ex} % Space below
  {\normalfont}                  % Body font (roman for definitions)
  {}                             % Indent amount
  {\bfseries}                    % Theorem head font
  {.}                            % Punctuation after theorem head
  {0.5em}                        % Space after theorem head
  {}                             % Theorem head spec

\theoremstyle{condensed}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[section]
\newtheorem{lemma}[theorem]{Lemma}
\newtheorem{proposition}[theorem]{Proposition}
\newtheorem{corollary}[theorem]{Corollary}
\newtheorem{conjecture}[theorem]{Conjecture}

\theoremstyle{condenseddef}
\newtheorem{definition}[theorem]{Definition}
\newtheorem{example}[theorem]{Example}
\newtheorem{remark}[theorem]{Remark}
\newtheorem{observation}[theorem]{Observation}

% `algorithmblock` (theorem-like) — separate from the `algorithm`
% float package, which is reserved for pseudocode floats elsewhere
% in the paper.
\newtheorem{algorithmblock}[theorem]{Algorithm}

% ── Proof environment formatting ───────────────────────────────────────────────
% Hollow square for QED, italic 'Proof' heading to distinguish from bold theorems
\renewcommand{\qedsymbol}{$\square$}
\makeatletter
\renewenvironment{proof}[1][\proofname]{\par
  \pushQED{\qed}%
  \normalfont \topsep0.8ex\@plus0.2ex\@minus0.1ex\relax
  \trivlist
  \item[\hskip\labelsep
        \itshape
    #1\@addpunct{.}]\ignorespaces
}{%
  \popQED\endtrivlist\@endpefalse
}
\makeatother

% ── LeanBlueprint macros ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
% These macros annotate theorem-like environments with Lean 4 declaration
% linkages.  They are consumed by the proof-objects extraction pipeline
% and (optionally) by leanblueprint/plasTeX for dependency graph generation.
%
% Usage:
%   \begin{theorem}\label{thm:my-result}
%     \lean{MyPaper.Chapter.my_result}      % Lean declaration name
%     \leanok                            % proof is sorry-free
%     \uses{def:prerequisite}            % dependency labels
%     Statement here.
%   \end{theorem}
% Repository identity — content-agnostic. A real build MUST inject the folio's
% own repo/pages base; the content pipeline (content/pipeline/render-latex.ts)
% does this per paper, or override at compile time via \renewcommand. The
% defaults below are deliberate placeholders, never a specific paper's repo.
\providecommand{\foliorepobase}{https://github.com/OWNER/REPO}
\providecommand{\foliopagesbase}{https://OWNER.github.io/REPO}
% Base URL for Lean documentation (doc-gen4 pages on GitHub Pages)
\newcommand{\leandocsbase}{\foliopagesbase/lean/}
% GitHub source URL for Lean files
\newcommand{\leansrcbase}{\foliorepobase/blob/main/lean/}
% Repo-scoped GitHub code-search base.  We only carry the declaration name
% (not a reliable file path), so the ∀ status mark links here: it lands on a
% GitHub view of the declaration's source within the repo.
\newcommand{\leansrcsearchbase}{\foliorepobase/search?q=}
%
% ── Lean formalisation-status palette ───────────────────────────────────────
% Single source of truth for the three-state ∀ colour code.  Tweak here.
% Orange is deliberately avoided: it reads poorly on white and sits too close
% to red.  The short text tag (stub/draft/ok) carries the status regardless of
% how distinguishable the colours are on a given display/print.
\colorlet{leanstubcolor}{BrickRed}     % stubbed  — sorry/placeholder, or QA-vacuous/trivial
\colorlet{leandraftcolor}{Purple}      % drafted  — genuine statement in Lean, not yet sorry-free
\colorlet{leanokcolor}{ForestGreen}    % compiled — built sorry-free
%
% Internal flag: tracks whether \lean was called in the current environment.
\newif\ifleantagged
%
% \lean{Decl.Name} — renders a clickable, bold ∀ icon linking to the Lean
% declaration's source on GitHub.  Standalone, this is the "drafted" state
% (statement stated in Lean); a following \leanok adds the green compiled mark.
\newcommand{\lean}[1]{%
  \global\leantaggedtrue%
  \texorpdfstring{%
    \href{\leansrcsearchbase#1}{%
      \textsuperscript{\textcolor{leandraftcolor}{$\boldsymbol{\forall}$}}%
    }%
  }{(Lean: #1)}%
}
%
% \leanok — marks environment as fully formalized (sorry-free).
% Renders a green checkmark.
\newcommand{\leanok}{%
  \texorpdfstring{%
    \textsuperscript{\textcolor{ForestGreen}{\checkmark}}%
  }{[proved]}%
}
%
% \notready — marks environment as not ready to formalize.
% Renders a red cross.
\newcommand{\notready}{%
  \texorpdfstring{%
    \textsuperscript{\textcolor{BrickRed}{$\times$}}%
  }{[not ready]}%
}
%
% \mathlibok — marks declarations merged into mathlib.
% Renders a dark-green double checkmark.
\newcommand{\mathlibok}{%
  \texorpdfstring{%
    \textsuperscript{\textcolor{OliveGreen}{\checkmark\kern-0.3em\checkmark}}%
  }{[mathlib]}%
}
\newcommand{\uses}[1]{}            % \uses{label1, label2, ...}
\newcommand{\proves}[1]{}          % \proves{thm:label} (in proof environments)
%
% ── Margin annotations: source links + issue tracker + structured comments ──
%
% Every labelled content block, section, and chapter carries a compact
% strip of clickable icons in the right margin:
%
%   ∀  → Lean docs page for this block's declaration (if any)
%   ∇  → .md source on GitHub (the narrative form, authoritative per CLAUDE.md)
%   #  → GitHub issues filtered by the block label (existing discussion)
%   +  → "Add comment / open new issue" pre-filled with the block label
%
% The macros below are pure LaTeX, no font dependencies. They are
% emitted by content/pipeline/render-latex.ts after each \label{}.
% Empty arguments hide the corresponding icon, so a block without a
% Lean ref still gets ∇ # +, etc.

% Base URLs.  Derived from \foliorepobase (injected per-folio); override at
% compile time via \renewcommand{...} if needed.
\newcommand{\trackerbase}{\foliorepobase/issues?q=}
\newcommand{\sourcebase}{\foliorepobase/blob/main/content/}
\newcommand{\commentbase}{\foliorepobase/issues/new?title=Comment+on+}

% \blockannot{label}{leanDecl}{mdRelPath}
% \blockannotok{label}{leanDecl}{mdRelPath}   — same but adds green ✓
%                                                indicating the Lean proof
%                                                is sorry-free.
% Compact horizontal strip of icons in the right margin. Any of the three
% positional args may be empty — that icon is simply omitted. The leading
% \mbox{} anchors the marginnote to a non-floating reference point in the
% body line so adjacent margin notes don't collide.
%
% NOTE: \makeatletter is required here so that \blockannot@i (and the
% internal \@tmp / \@empty refs in its body) are tokenised with @ as a
% letter (catcode 11).  Without it, \blockannot@i is tokenised as
% \blockannot (catcode-12 @ stops the control-word scan), which causes
% "Command \blockannot already defined" and a subsequent parameter-stack
% overflow when \blockannot recurses into itself.
% \leanstatusmark{status}{decl} — the Lean formalisation indicator: a BOLD,
% colour-coded ∀ plus a short text tag, the whole thing hyperlinked to the
% declaration's source on GitHub.  The tag makes the status legible even when
% the colours are hard to tell apart on a given display or in print.
%   status = stubbed  → red    ∀ stub   (sorry/placeholder, or vacuous/trivial per QA)
%   status = drafted  → purple ∀ draft  (genuine statement in Lean, not yet sorry-free)
%   status = compiled → green  ∀ ok     (built sorry-free)
\makeatletter
\newcommand{\leanstatusmark}[2]{%
  \def\lsm@s{#1}%
  \def\lsm@stub{stubbed}\def\lsm@comp{compiled}%
  \ifx\lsm@s\lsm@stub
    \def\lsm@col{leanstubcolor}\def\lsm@tag{stub}%
  \else\ifx\lsm@s\lsm@comp
    \def\lsm@col{leanokcolor}\def\lsm@tag{ok}%
  \else
    \def\lsm@col{leandraftcolor}\def\lsm@tag{draft}%
  \fi\fi
  \href{\leansrcsearchbase #2}{%
    \textcolor{\lsm@col}{$\boldsymbol{\forall}$\,\textbf{\tiny\lsm@tag}}%
  }%
}
% \blockannot[status]{label}{leanDecl}{mdRelPath}
%   Optional status keyword (default "drafted") drives the ∀ colour + tag.
% \blockannotok{label}{leanDecl}{mdRelPath}  ==  \blockannot[compiled]{...}
%   (kept for back-compat with previously generated content).
\newcommand{\blockannot}[4][drafted]{\blockannot@i{#1}{#2}{#3}{#4}}
\newcommand{\blockannotok}[3]{\blockannot@i{compiled}{#1}{#2}{#3}}
\newcommand{\blockannot@i}[4]{%
  \mbox{}\marginnote{%
    \raggedright\scriptsize
    \ifx\relax#3\relax\else
      \leanstatusmark{#1}{#3}\,%
    \fi
    \ifx\relax#4\relax\else
      \href{\sourcebase #4}{\textcolor{NavyBlue}{$\nabla$}}\,%
    \fi
    \ifx\relax#2\relax\else
      \href{\trackerbase #2}{\textcolor{NavyBlue}{\#}}\,%
      \href{\commentbase #2}{\textcolor{NavyBlue}{$+$}}%
    \fi
  }%
}
\makeatother

% \chapterannot{chapterDir}{trackerLabel}
% Chapter-level annotation: link to the chapter directory + tracker.
\newcommand{\chapterannot}[2]{%
  \mbox{}\marginnote{%
    \raggedright\scriptsize
    \href{\sourcebase #1/}{\textcolor{NavyBlue}{$\nabla$ src}}\\[-0.3ex]%
    \href{\trackerbase #2}{\textcolor{NavyBlue}{\# issues}}\\[-0.3ex]%
    \href{\commentbase #2}{\textcolor{NavyBlue}{$+$ note}}%
  }%
}

% \sectionannot{label} — section-level annotation: tracker only.
\newcommand{\sectionannot}[1]{%
  \marginnote{%
    \raggedright\scriptsize
    \href{\trackerbase #1}{\textcolor{NavyBlue}{\#}}\,%
    \href{\commentbase #1}{\textcolor{NavyBlue}{$+$}}%
  }%
}

% Back-compat: \tracker{label} still works (subsumed by \blockannot but kept
% so old hand-written .md content references don't break).
\newcommand{\tracker}[1]{\blockannot{#1}{}{}}

% \bcomment[author]{text} — structured human/agent comment in the margin.
% `text` empty → renders an "(add note)" stub. Optional [author] tag appears
% as a small "— Author" suffix.  Renders in BrickRed to distinguish from
% the auto-generated annotation icons.
\newcommand{\bcomment}[2][]{%
  \marginnote{%
    \raggedright\scriptsize\textcolor{BrickRed}{%
      \textbf{note:}~%
      \ifx\relax#2\relax\textit{(add note)}\else#2\fi%
      \ifx\relax#1\relax\else~\textemdash~\textit{#1}\fi%
    }%
  }%
}
%
% ── Glossary terms: \defterm{} / \refterm{} ─────────────────────────────────
% PDF rendering is intentionally clean — the HTML viewer carries the
% interactive affordance (dotted underline on hover, click-to-jump).
%
%   \defterm{slug}{Visible}  defining occurrence: bold-italic + invisible
%                            \phantomsection\label{term:slug} target
%   \refterm{slug}{Visible}  referencing occurrence: invisible
%                            \hyperref[term:slug]{Visible} (no decoration)
%
% Single-arg forms \defterm{slug} / \refterm{slug} use the slug as the
% visible label (the common case where slug == display text).
% NOTE: defined as \DeclareRobustCommand (not \newcommand) so the
% macros do not expand prematurely in moving arguments such as
% section titles.  The bare \newcommand form caused titlesec to
% recurse expanding `\refterm{descent}` inside a subsubsection
% title until the input stack overflowed — Build & Publish #3262
% failed with "TeX capacity exceeded [input stack size=10000]"
% expanding that exact macro on l.3752 of the rendered chapter.
% \texorpdfstring keeps PDF bookmarks safe by stripping the link.
\makeatletter
\DeclareRobustCommand{\defterm}[1]{\@ifnextchar\bgroup{\defterm@two{#1}}{\defterm@one{#1}}}
\newcommand{\defterm@one}[1]{\phantomsection\label{term:#1}\textbf{\emph{#1}}}
\newcommand{\defterm@two}[2]{\phantomsection\label{term:#1}\textbf{\emph{#2}}}
\DeclareRobustCommand{\refterm}[1]{\@ifnextchar\bgroup{\refterm@two{#1}}{\refterm@one{#1}}}
\newcommand{\refterm@one}[1]{\texorpdfstring{\hyperref[term:#1]{#1}}{#1}}
\newcommand{\refterm@two}[2]{\texorpdfstring{\hyperref[term:#1]{#2}}{#2}}
\makeatother

\newcommand{\proofstatuslegend}{%

  \par\smallskip\noindent
  \begin{tabular}{@{}cl@{\qquad}cl@{}}
    \textcolor{leanstubcolor}{$\boldsymbol{\forall}$\,\textbf{\footnotesize stub}}
      & Stub: \texttt{sorry}/placeholder, or vacuous/trivial per QA
    & \textcolor{leandraftcolor}{$\boldsymbol{\forall}$\,\textbf{\footnotesize draft}}
      & Drafted: genuine statement in Lean, not yet sorry-free\\
    \textcolor{leanokcolor}{$\boldsymbol{\forall}$\,\textbf{\footnotesize ok}}
      & Compiled: built sorry-free
    & \textcolor{OliveGreen}{\checkmark\kern-0.3em\checkmark} & Merged into Mathlib\\
  \end{tabular}\bigskip
}

(15) & $\varphi_{01}L_+\allowbreak{} \cdot \psi_1\sigma_1$ & $\varphi_{01}\psi_1\sigma_0 +\allowbreak{} \varphi_{01}\psi_1 h\,L_+\allowbreak{}$ & \textbf{Twist meets vertical polarization.} Via $\sigma_0\sigma_1 \cdot \sigma_1 =\allowbreak{} \sigma_0\sigma_1^2 =\allowbreak{} \sigma_0(h\sigma_1 +\allowbreak{} \mathbf{1}) =\allowbreak{} h L_+\allowbreak{} + \sigma_0$: the twist absorbs the vertical crossing (Hecke relation on $\sigma_1^2$) and emits the orthogonal polarization $\sigma_0$. (16) & $\varphi_{01}L_+ \cdot \psi_{01}L_+$ & $\varphi_{01}\psi_{01} L_-\allowbreak{} + \varphi_{01}\psi_{01} h\,e^-\allowbreak{}$ & \textbf{Two Hopf dressings collide.} Via $(\sigma_0\sigma_1)^2 = L_- + he^-$: the self-product of the Hopf link produces the reversed link $L_-$ plus an electron channel weighted by $h$. Two pre-twisted photons interacting through their twist content alone generate both chirality reversal and pair production. \\

5 & \textbf{HOMFLYPT} $P(K; a, z)$ & $\mathbb{Z}[a^{\pm 1}, z^{\pm 1}]$ & $\{P(K; q_0^{N-1}, h_q)\}_{N \geq 2} \in \mathbb{R}^\infty$ & $P(\bar K) = P(K;\, a^{-1}, z)$ (mirror symmetry; chirality for all SU($N$)) & $\{P(\bar K; q_0^{N-1}, h_q)\}_{N} =\allowbreak{} \{P(K; q_0^{-(N-1)}, h_q)\}_N$ — the \textbf{mirror family}: same SU($N$) tower evaluated at $q_0^{-(N-1)}$. Difference $P - P_{\mathrm{mirror}}$ is the CPT-violating observable per channel & \textbf{Family of observables indexed by $N$} & \textbf{not built} \\
6 & Colored Jones $J_K^{(V)}(q)$ & per-irrep polynomial & $J_K^{(V)}(q_0) \in \mathbb{R}$ per $V$ & $J_K^{(V^*)}$ (representation dual; particle/antiparticle) & $J_K^{(V^*)}(q_0) \in \mathbb{R}$ — the contragredient-representation invariant; for self-dual $V = V^*$ this equals $J_K^{(V)}$ (bosonic channel) & Per-representation channel & not built \\
7 & Wedderburn decomposition $\{\dim_q V_\lambda\}$ & $\mathbb{R}^{\vert \mathrm{Part}(n)\vert }$ & $\{\dim_{q_0} V_\lambda\}$ & $\{\dim_q V_{\lambda'}\}$ (conjugate partition; Young transpose) & $\{\dim_{q_0} V_{\lambda'}\}$ — the conjugate-partition quantum dimensions; $\dim_q V_\lambda =\allowbreak{} \dim_q V_{\lambda'}$ iff $\lambda$ is self-conjugate & Per-partition quantum dimensions & implemented \\
8 & Frobenius pairing $y_\lambda \chi_\lambda$ & weight decomposition & $y_\lambda(q_0) \cdot \chi_\lambda(\beta)(q_0)$ & dual basis $y^*_\lambda$ (Frobenius self-duality; weight $\leftrightarrow$ character) & $y^*_\lambda(q_0) \cdot \chi^*_\lambda(\beta)(q_0)$ — the dual-weight / dual-character product; by Frobenius self-duality $y^* = y$ and $\chi^* = \chi$, so this is \emph{the same observable} (the pairing is self-dual) & Per-partition mass contributions & implemented \\
9 & LP/SDP shadow prices $y^*$ & dual variables & $y^*(q_0) \in \mathbb{R}^m$ & primal $x$ (LP strong duality; binding-energy shadow prices) & $x^*(q_0) \in \mathbb{R}^n$ — the primal optimal allocation; by strong duality $\sum t_i x_i^* =\allowbreak{} n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot y_0^*$, so primal and dual carry the same total but in complementary coordinates & Binding-energy shadow prices & implemented \\
10 & Kauffman bracket $\langle K \rangle(A)$ & $\mathbb{Z}[A^{\pm 1}]$ & $\langle K \rangle(q_0^{1/4}) \in \mathbb{R}$ & $\langle \bar K \rangle$ (mirror bracket; writhe conjugation) & $\langle \bar K \rangle(q_0^{1/4}) =\allowbreak{} \langle K \rangle(q_0^{-1/4}) \in \mathbb{R}$ — mirror bracket at inverse root & Unnormalized Jones & partially (hardcoded knots) \\
11 & Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K(t)$ & $\mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1}]$ & $\Delta_K(q_0) \in \mathbb{R}$ & $\Delta_K(t^{-1}) = \Delta_K(t)$ (Fox calculus; fibered $\leftrightarrow$ non-fibered) & $\Delta_K(q_0^{-1}) =\allowbreak{} \Delta_K(q_0) \in \mathbb{R}$ — \textbf{self-dual} (Alexander is palindromic); the categorical dual is the \emph{same observable} & HOMFLYPT at $N \to \infty$ & not built explicitly \\
12 & Khovanov homology $H^{i,j}(K)$ & bigraded $\mathbb{Z}$-module & Euler char $\to$ Jones & $H_{i,j}$ (Poincaré duality; categorified mirror) & Poincaré-dual ranks $\to$ same Euler characteristic $\to$ same Jones value. The categorified dual carries \emph{torsion} information invisible to the Euler characteristic & Categorified Jones & not built (out of scope) \\
13 & Knot group $\pi_1(S^3 \setminus K)$ & finitely-presented group & ? & peripheral system (Dehn surgery duality) & ? — the peripheral system $(m, \ell)$ under $\tau$ is an open question; its image would encode the longitude/meridian structure of the knot complement at $q_0$ & Open question & open \\

\par\bigskip\noindent\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}\par\nobreak\smallskip
\noindent{\small\ttfamily [stochastic-mechanics]~\#23}\par\nobreak\smallskip
\noindent
\begin{tabular}{l>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.756\linewidth}}
\toprule
Symbol & Reading \\
\midrule
$\mathbf{No}$ & The class of surreal numbers (Conway 1976). Contains $\mathbb{R}$ as a proper subclass plus infinite and infinitesimal elements. \\
$\omega$ & The surreal representation of the first infinite ordinal. $\omega > n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ (but $\omega - 1$, $\omega/2$, $\sqrt{\omega}$, $\ldots$ are also infinite surreals — there is no smallest infinite surreal). Concretely, $\omega =\allowbreak{} \{\,0, 1, 2, \dots \,\mid\,\,\}$ in Conway's $\{L \mid R\}$ form. \\
$\varepsilon$ & The positive infinitesimal defined as $1/\omega$. $0 < \varepsilon < 1/n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ (but $\varepsilon/2$, $\varepsilon^2$, $\ldots$ are also infinitesimal — there is no smallest positive infinitesimal). The substrate parameter $q$ in this paper is built from $\varepsilon$ via \hyperref[def:q-from-epsilon]{the $q$-from-$\varepsilon$ relation}. \\
$1 + \varepsilon$ & An \textbf{infinitesimal lift} of $1$. The "relax strict equalities to $1 + \varepsilon$" pattern in the appendix \hyperref[sec:relaxing-strict-equalities]{(\texttt{sec:\allowbreak{}relaxing-\allowbreak{}strict-\allowbreak{}equalities})} replaces every $x = 1$ with $x = 1 + \varepsilon$ for some surreal infinitesimal $\varepsilon$. \\
$\mathrm{st}\!:\,\mathbf{No}_{\text{fin}} \to\allowbreak{} \mathbb{R}$ & The \textbf{standard-part functor} on finite (non-infinite) surreals — sends $1 + \varepsilon$ to $1$, sends $\omega^{-1}$ to $0$, sends every finite real to itself. Replaces the classical limit; see \hyperref[sec:standard-part-classical-limits]{\texttt{sec:\allowbreak{}standard-\allowbreak{}part-\allowbreak{}classical-\allowbreak{}limits}}. \\
$\mathrm{ord}_\omega\,x$ & The \textbf{$\omega$-adic order} — leading exponent of $x$ in Conway normal form. Direct surreal analogue of $\mathrm{ord}_p$ in $p$-adic analysis. Used to grade $\mathcal{H}_q$ and to formulate Goncharov-period-depth identifications. \\
$\{L \mid R\}$ & Conway's \textbf{simplest-form construction}: a surreal whose left set is $L$ and right set is $R$. Birthday-graded; the surreal's complexity is the minimum number of construction steps from $\{\,\mid\,\} = 0$. \\
$b(x)$ & \textbf{Birthday} of a surreal $x$ — the ordinal at which $x$ first appears in the Conway construction. $b(0) = 0$, $b(1) = b(-1) = 1$, $b(\omega) = \omega$, $b(\varepsilon) = \omega$. \\
$a \sim b$ & $a$ and $b$ have the \textbf{same standard part} — i.e. $a - b$ is infinitesimal (or zero). Used in Millennium-bound statements: the surreal bound holds \textbf{up to a $1 + \varepsilon$ multiplier}, which collapses to equality under $\mathrm{st}$. \\
$a \prec b$ & $a$ is \textbf{infinitesimal relative to} $b$, i.e. $\vert a/b\vert $ is infinitesimal. Conway's asymptotic-domination order. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\par

\begin{tabular}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.305\linewidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.305\linewidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.305\linewidth}}
\toprule
Concept & Font & Symbols \\
\midrule
Crossing energy & plain italic & $E_{\mathfrak{H}}$ — total crossing energy of hadron $\mathfrak{H}$. $E_{\mathfrak{H}} =\allowbreak{} \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{H}} \cdot c_q^2$. \\
Hook-length product & Latin cap + arg & $H_q(\lambda) =\allowbreak{} \prod_{x \in \lambda} [h_x(\lambda)]_q$ — always with partition argument. \\
Iwahori–Hecke algebra & Latin cap & $H_n(q)$ — always with subscript $n$. \\
Atomic braid word & calligraphic & $\mathcal{B}_K \in H_{3A}(q)$ — canonical atomic braid for atom $K = (Z, N)$ with $A = Z + N$. Factorises as $\mathcal{B}_K =\allowbreak{} \mathcal{B}_K^{\mathrm{vac}} \cdot \bowtie_K$ (vacuum · interface). Relocated from $\beta_K$ to cal in Phase 5n — cal register expanded to admit Hecke-algebra structural elements alongside bundles/sheaves. \\
Vacuum (constit) factor & calligraphic + superscript & $\mathcal{B}_K^{\mathrm{vac}} =\allowbreak{} \mathcal{B}_p^{(1)} \cdots \mathcal{B}_p^{(Z)} \mathcal{B}_n^{(1)} \cdots \mathcal{B}_n^{(N)}$ — disjoint Hecke product of per-nucleon 3-strand blocks (no interface generators), i.e. "constituent vacuum". Phase 5n synonym for the historical $\beta_K^{\mathrm{constit}}$ of . \\
Proton / neutron H\_3 braid & calligraphic & $\mathcal{B}_p, \mathcal{B}_n \in H_3(q)$ — canonical 3-strand intra-nucleon braids (quark content u-u-d / u-d-d). Relocated from $\beta_p, \beta_n$ in Phase 5n. \\
Intra-atom interface operator & bowtie + K subscript & $\bowtie_K$ — K-deformed Hopf-link-style operator at strand-block boundaries of atom $K$; $\mathcal{B}_K =\allowbreak{} \mathcal{B}_K^{\mathrm{vac}} \cdot \bowtie_K$. Always adorned with $K$ subscript (no bare $\bowtie$ for this concept). Phase 5n replacement for $\Delta_I^K$. \\
Inter-block Hopf-link operation & $\oplus$ & $X \oplus Y$ — Hopf-link / fusion of two composite structures (e.g., $Z\mathfrak{p} \oplus N\mathfrak{n}$ = Z proton blocks Hopf-linked with N neutron blocks). Relocated from bare $\bowtie$ in Phase 5n to disambiguate from intra-atom $\bowtie_K$. \\
Hopf link object & calligraphic & $\mathcal{L}_K$, $\mathcal{L}_H$ — the Hopf link as a knot/link object. $\mathcal{L}_H$ is the standard Hopf link in the appendix mass-formula notation; $\mathcal{L}_K$ is the K-parameterized variant. \\
Frobenius Gram matrix & upright cap + arg & $\mathrm{G}(q) \in \mathrm{Mat}_N(R)$ — Gram matrix of the chosen N-element Frobenius basis at Hecke parameter $q$, with R the Hecke base ring (not $\mathbb{R}$). Currently a \textbf{matrix-valued function} $\mathrm{G}: \mathbb{R} \to\allowbreak{} \mathrm{Mat}_N(R)$, $q \mapsto \mathrm{G}(q)$; promotion to a functor (with Reeb source category) is aspirational pending formalization of Reeb as a category. Upright distinguishes from gravitational scalar $G_q$ (italic, q-subscript). \\
Markov trace & upright lc + M & $\mathrm{tr}_M$ — Jones–Markov trace on $H_n(q)$; $\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K) =\allowbreak{} \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi^\lambda(\mathcal{B}_K)$. Lowercase upright matches QOU's universal \texttt{\textbackslash\{\}mathrm\{tr\}} convention (1489+ uses, parallel to $\det$, $\dim$, $\mathrm{Hom}$). Distinct from fibre functor $\tau$ (italic Greek). \\
Jones–Markov central coefficient & plain italic & $y_\lambda$ — coefficient in $\mathrm{tr}_M =\allowbreak{} \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi_\lambda$, given by Wenzl's hook–content closed form [wenzl1988]. Sign-indefinite at $n \geq 4$. Distinct from the Plancherel measure $w_\lambda$ and the q-deformed Wedderburn-block weight $\tilde w_\lambda$ at $q \neq 1$ — coincides with $w_\lambda$ only on the self-conjugate stratum (see \href{../braids-and-knots/wedderburn-weight-canonical.md}{\texttt{prop:\allowbreak{}wedderburn-\allowbreak{}weight-\allowbreak{}canonical}}). Never confuse with $u_\lambda$ (LP shadow-price). \\
LP shadow-price & plain italic & $u_\lambda, u_0$ — Schrijver linear-programming convention for operator-selection LP dual variables. Non-negative by LP duality. Never write $y_\lambda$ here. \\
Markov parameter & plain italic & $z = 1/(\check{q} + \check{q}^{-1})$ — equivalently $1/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})$. \\
Mass (knot) & fraktur & $\mathfrak{m}_{\mathcal{K}}$ — knot mass. \\
Plancherel measure (classical) & plain italic & $w_\lambda :=\allowbreak{} (\dim V_\lambda)^2 / n!$ — the classical Plancherel probability measure on partitions $\lambda \vdash n$, with $\dim V_\lambda$ the $q$-independent (classical) Hecke-irrep dimension (= number of standard Young tableaux of shape $\lambda$). Sums to $1$ exactly in $\mathbb{Q}$. See \href{../braids-and-knots/plancherel-weight-boundedness.md}{\texttt{prop:\allowbreak{}plancherel-\allowbreak{}weight-\allowbreak{}boundedness}}. \textbf{Distinct} from the q-deformed Wedderburn-block weight $\tilde w_\lambda$; the two coincide at $q = 1$ only. \\
Quantum dimension & plain italic & $\dim_q(\lambda) =\allowbreak{} [n]_q! / \prod_{x \in \lambda} [h_x]_q$ — the $q$-deformed Frame–Robinson–Thrall hook-length dimension. Reduces to $\dim V_\lambda$ at $q = 1$. Used in the q-deformed Wedderburn-block weight $\tilde w_\lambda =\allowbreak{} \dim_q^2(\lambda)/[n]_q!$. \\
Spinor information rate & plain italic with háček & $\check{q}$ — eigenvalue of the elementary half-twist on the spin-½ fundamental rep of $\mathrm{SU}_q(2)$, $\check{q}^2 = q$. The "rate per half-twist" along a single linear braid (no surface area). Analogous to $i: -1$ as $\check{q}: q$ — the algebraic ingredient that lifts the 1-D adjoint braid algebra to the 2-D spinor (spin-½) representation. The háček (Czech, "little hook") encodes the relation $\check{q}^2 = q$ in the glyph. \textbf{Renamed from $r$ on 2026-06-04} (freed $r$ for radius / generic-real contexts; absorbed the historical Habiro $u = q^{1/2}$ literature name). \textbf{Never} use $r$, $t$ (clashes with $V_K(t)$ knot variable), $\iota$ (clashes with involution / inclusion), or bare $u$ for $q^{1/2}$. \\
Wedderburn-block weight (q-deformed) & plain italic with tilde & $\tilde w_\lambda :=\allowbreak{} \dim_q^2(\lambda) / [n]_q!$ — the q-deformed analogue of the classical Plancherel measure $w_\lambda$. \textbf{Not} a probability measure at $q \neq 1$: empirically $\sum_\lambda \tilde w_\lambda \approx\allowbreak{} 1.51$ at $q_0 = 1.109978595554181\ldots$ (50 dps) for $n = 12$. Specialises to $w_\lambda$ at $q = 1$. Used in \href{../braids-and-knots/plancherel-term-7-formulation.md}{\texttt{prop:\allowbreak{}plancherel-\allowbreak{}term-\allowbreak{}7-\allowbreak{}formulation}} and the q-deformed Wedderburn-block normalisation of \href{../braids-and-knots/wedderburn-weight-canonical.md}{\texttt{prop:\allowbreak{}wedderburn-\allowbreak{}weight-\allowbreak{}canonical}}. \textbf{Never} call this "Plancherel weight" without the tilde — the classical Plancherel $w_\lambda$ is a different, smaller object. \\
Wenzl principal-spec length & Greek & $\ell$ — number of points in the Schur principal specialisation $s_\lambda(1, q^2, q^4, \ldots, q^{2(\ell-1)})$ defining $y_\lambda$ via Wenzl's formula. \textbf{Renamed from $r_W$} in the May 2026 cleanup (then-current spinor rate was $r$); $r$ itself was subsequently renamed to $\check{q}$ on 2026-06-04. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

Primitive root of unity & Greek + sub & $\zeta_n := e^{2\pi i / n}$ — primitive $n$-th root of unity. \textbf{Always with subscript:} $\zeta_5$ for Bring $S_5$-symmetry shape, $\zeta_6 = e^{i\pi/3}$ for figure-8 ideal-tetrahedron shape. \textbf{Never bare $\zeta$} (collides with Riemann zeta $\zeta(s)$ — always parenthesised — and with character $\chi_\zeta$ — always with $\chi$ prefix). \\
Vortex morphism & Greek & $\varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A$ — generic closed vortex. Never $\gamma$ for a vortex; $\gamma$ is reserved (photon, Euler–Mascheroni constant, Dirac matrices). \\
Hahn–Exton q-Bessel & italic + sub/super & $J_\nu^{(3)}(x;q)$ — matrix coefficient of the quantum motion group $E_q(2)$ (the $\mathrm{SU}_q(2)\to E_q(2)$ contraction); its power-series coefficients are the $c_k$ precision ladder (\href{../mass-theory/q-beta-c-k-recursion-from-habiro-q-difference.md}{\texttt{prop:\allowbreak{}q-\allowbreak{}beta-\allowbreak{}c-\allowbreak{}k-\allowbreak{}recursion-\allowbreak{}from-\allowbreak{}habiro-\allowbreak{}q-\allowbreak{}difference}}). \textbf{Subscript $\nu$ = order; never bare $J$} — collides with the Jones polynomial $J_K(q)$ (subscript a knot $K$). The bar-graded Jacobi–Anger weights are ordinary Bessel $J_n(x)$ (integer order). \\
q-Lommel polynomial & italic & $h_{n,\nu}(x;q)$ — degree-$n$ polynomial from iterating the q-Bessel order contiguity $J_{\nu+1}=b_\nu J_\nu - J_{\nu-1}$; its (algebraic) zeros are the truncated q-Bessel zeros (the "tower from two seeds"). Distinct from the hook-length $H_q(\lambda)$ and the heat-decay rate $\mu_\lambda$. \\
\bottomrule

\noindent{\small\ttfamily [appendix-transfer-matrices]~\#1}\par\nobreak\smallskip
\noindent
\begin{tabular}{l>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.27\linewidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.575\linewidth}}
\toprule
Symbol & Name & Definition \\
\midrule
$q$ & Substrate parameter & A real number $q > 1$ (the single free parameter of the theory) \\
$s$ & Skein amplitude & $s = q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2}$ \\
$z$ & Markov parameter & $z(q) =\allowbreak{} \dfrac{1}{q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}}$ \\
$\sigma_i$ & Braid / Hecke generator & Generator of the braid group $B_n$ and its image in $H_n(q)$ (same symbol); in the latter satisfies the Hecke relation $\sigma_i^2 =\allowbreak{} (q -\allowbreak{} q^{-1})\sigma_i +\allowbreak{} 1$ \\
$J_K(q)$ & Jones polynomial & Knot invariant of knot $K$, polynomial in $q^{\pm 1}$ \\
$\mathrm{M}_2(R)$ & $2 \times 2$ matrices & Over ring $R = \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}]$ \\
$\mathbb{I}$ & Identity matrix & $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

Frobenius / Hopf & survives & survives + Frobenius twist $a^p = a$ for nilpotents \\
Markov trace / Jones polynomial & survives & survives (modular Jones) \\
Wedderburn semisimplicity & survives & \textbf{fails} at $q = \zeta_p$ (cells, not blocks) \\
Tannaka reconstruction & survives & survives in modular Tannakian form \\
Standard part to $\mathbb{R}$ & survives & \textbf{none} — no archimedean reduction \\
Brauer characters & not needed & needed (replace ordinary characters) \\
Birthday grading & ordinal-valued & $p$-adic-ordinal-valued \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\noindent{\small\ttfamily [appendix-surreals-archimedean]~\#4}\par\nobreak\smallskip
\noindent
\begin{tabular}{l>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.34\linewidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.27\linewidth}}
\toprule
 & Hausdorff recurrence & Collatz dynamics \\
\midrule
\textbf{Space} & $q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ & $\Phi \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ \\
\textbf{Map} & $F(q) = (q^2-q+1)/q$ & $\Phi \mapsto\allowbreak{} \Phi +\allowbreak{} \log_q([3]/[2]^v)$ \\
\textbf{Fixed point} & $q = 1$ & $\Phi = 0$ (i.e., $P = 1$) \\
\textbf{Step size} & $\hbar_q = (q-1)/q$ & $\vert \Delta\Phi\vert  \approx 2.76$ \\
\textbf{Contraction ratio} & $F'(q) = 1 - 1/q^2$ & $R(v) = [3]_q / [2]_q^v$ \\
\textbf{At fixed point} & $F'(1) = 0$ — \textbf{superattracting} & $R(2) \approx 3/4$ — \textbf{uniform} \\
\textbf{Convergence} & Superlinear ($3$ steps from $q_0$) & Linear ($\Phi_0/2.76$ cycles) \\
\textbf{Entropy per step} & $\eta_q / \vert F'(q)\vert \to\allowbreak{} \infty$ at $q = 1$ & $3\eta_q \approx \text{const}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
